problem: Existing embodied navigation benchmarks (VLN and object-goal) report performance only under clean inputs. They neglect depth-sensor corruptions, realistic instruction variations and prompt attacks, and offer no unified framework to compare robustness mitigation strategies.
motivation: Real-world deployment involves sensor degradation (low light, blur, depth noise, missing depth) and varied or adversarial user instructions, and agents are known to fail under minor perturbations. A unified benchmark that compares each corrupted episode to its clean counterpart is needed to diagnose failure modes and to test which fixes actually help.
key_idea: NavTrust is a unified benchmark that corrupts RGB, depth and instructions for seven VLN and object-goal navigation agents, and compares four mitigation strategies (data augmentation, teacher-student distillation, adapters, safeguard LLM) in simulation and on a real robot.
insight: Depth-using agents are more robust to RGB corruption than RGB-only agents, but they are very fragile to depth corruption, and the fusion design matters (WMNav's late fusion with confidence gating beats ETPNav's early fusion in PRS-SPL, 0.86 vs 0.79). Different mitigations fit different modalities: per-episode data augmentation is best for RGB (PRS-SR 0.92-0.94), while teacher-student distillation (0.85) and depth adapters (0.89) are much better for depth than augmentation (0.67-0.75). For language, a safeguard LLM that canonicalizes instructions gives large gains (PRS-SR +0.14/+0.20/+0.32 with fine-tuned LLaMA 3.2 for NaVid, Uni-NaVid and ETPNav).
method: RGB corruptions: eight camera-failure types (motion blur, low-light with or without CMOS noise, spatter, flare, defocus, foreign object, black-out), adapted from ImageNet-C and EnvEdit, at severity s=0.5 by default.
Depth corruptions: four novel types (Gaussian noise, missing data, multipath, quantization) modelling indoor depth-sensor failures.

Instruction corruptions: LLaMA-3.1 style rewrites (friendly, novice, professional, formal), spaCy-based capitalization, [MASK] token masking, black-box malicious prefixes, and white-box malicious system-prompt injection.

Protocol and metrics: HM3D val-unseen for object-goal navigation, R2R and RxR for VLN, with start and goal locations aligned across tasks; SR, SPL and the Performance Retention Score (PRS = mean over corruptions of corrupted/clean metric).

Data augmentation and teacher-student distillation: per-frame, per-episode and success-rate-distributed corruption sampling during ETPNav training; a student learns from an augmentation-trained teacher via imitation, policy-KL and feature-MSE losses.
Adapters: residual bottleneck ConvAdapters (about 4% of parameters) on the frozen depth and RGB encoders, with reliability-weighted fusion of panoramic view embeddings.
Safeguard LLM: an 8-bit fine-tuned LLaMA 3.2 (or prompt-engineered OpenAI o3) that sanitizes and canonicalizes instructions into RxR-style text once per episode.

setting.backbone: Seven evaluated agents: ETPNav, NaVid-7B, Uni-NaVid (VLN); WMNav, L3MVN, PSL, VLFM (object-goal). Mitigations applied on ETPNav (RGB-depth) and on all three VLN models (instruction, via LLaMA 3.2 8-bit fine-tuned or OpenAI o3).
setting.model_size: NaVid-7B; LLaMA 3.2 (8-bit) safeguard; adapters about 4% of ETPNav parameters
setting.training_data: Benchmark: agents are used as released. Mitigations: ETPNav trained with corruption augmentation on a subset of R2R; the safeguard LLaMA is fine-tuned to canonicalize instructions into RxR form (scale not specified).
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB, RGB-D or panoramic RGB-D depending on the agent, plus language instructions for VLN
setting.action_space: ETPNav: topological waypoints. Uni-NaVid/NaVid: low-level forward/turn actions. Object-goal agents: frontier/map-based exploration. Real robot: forward, turn left, turn right steps.
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D / HM3D scenes; R2R, RxR, HM3D ObjectNav)

numbers_note: The main SR/SPL/PRS results are shown only in figures (heatmaps), so no exact per-agent numbers can be copied. Mitigation results for ETPNav on R2R are given in the text and Table 1 as PRS-SR and per-corruption SR, which do not fit the benchmark-level SR/SPL format. Clean values appear only in fragments (e.g. ETPNav 65% SR on R2R, VLFM 50% SR).
results: Corruptions cause large degradation. RGB-only agents drop 22-31% SR under black-out and low-light with noise. Depth Gaussian noise collapses L3MVN from 50% to 2% SR and VLFM from 50% to 0%. VLFM is the most robust to RGB corruption (PRS 0.94). Mitigation: per-episode data augmentation at higher intensity reaches PRS-SR 0.94 for RGB and 0.75 for depth, distillation reaches 0.93 for RGB and 0.85 for depth, and depth adapters reach 0.89; the safeguard LLM raises instruction PRS-SR by up to 0.32. Real-robot trials show the same trends, e.g. ETPNav with augmentation cut steps from 50 to 42 under low-light with noise.
limitations: Only RGB, depth and instruction corruptions are covered, with a single default severity of 0.5. Motion and dynamics failures (pose noise, wheel slip) are excluded, and the real-world evaluation is a small number of trials measured by step count.

Mitigations are tested only on ETPNav (RGB-depth) and on the VLN models (instructions), since the other agents are training-free or lack public training code. RGB adapters failed because of encoder incompatibility.
Many explanations for the observed trends (e.g. early vs late fusion, tokenizer rigidity) are speculative and not isolated by ablation.
